content: Side Effects: Burning, stinging, swelling, irritation, redness, pimple-like bumps, tenderness, or flaking of the treated skin may occur. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, it is because they have determined that the benefits to you outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, this is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Precautions: Before using miconazole, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other azole antifungals (such as clotrimazole, econazole, or ketoconazole), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is not known whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: This medication may be harmful if swallowed. If someone has overdosed and is experiencing serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. If your doctor has directed you to use this medication, use it only for your current condition. Special Notes for Pityriasis Treatment: When treating pityriasis, this medication may not immediately restore normal skin color. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and use your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Different brands of this medication may have different storage requirements. Check the product package for instructions on how to store your specific brand, or ask your pharmacist. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. How to Use: This medication is for use on the skin only. Clean and thoroughly dry the area to be treated. Apply the medication to the affected skin, usually twice a day or as directed by your doctor. If using the spray form, shake the bottle well before applying. The dosage and length of treatment depend on the type of infection being treated. Do not apply this medication more often than prescribed. Apply enough medication to cover the affected area and some of the surrounding skin. After applying, wash your hands. Use this medication regularly to achieve the best results. Continue using it for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms disappear after a few days.
